channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) Explained
item.description: The key gas fingerprint, the five-step DGA test workflow, why one number never proves a fault, and a field checklist with reference standards.

item.title: Power System Protection Relays: The Complete Reference Guide
item.description: The relay operation workflow, five competing design goals, every relay category by measured quantity and by equipment, IEC 61850 architecture, inverse-time curves, coordination principles and a selection table.

item.title: LV Panel Types Explained: Switchgear, MCC, PFC, VFD, Feeder Pillar & More
item.description: Every panel you'll find in a low-voltage electrical system — MDB, PCC, SDB/DB, MCC, VFD panel, APFC/PFC panel, feeder pillar, busbar trunking, ATS/AMF and PLC panels — what each does, where it sits, and the IEC 61439 parts behind it.

item.title: 33/11 kV Substation: Single Line Diagram & Equipment Overview
item.description: How a 33/11 kV substation is built, walked through its single line diagram from incoming line to distribution feeders — every major equipment item, its function, and the protection schemes that back it up.

item.title: MCB, MCCB, ACB, RCCB & More: Electrical Switchgear & Protection Devices Explained
item.description: MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, SF6 breakers, RCCB, RCBO, ELCB, isolators, contactors, relays, fuses, SPDs and busbars — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: Gas Insulated Substation (GIS) Explained
item.description: A GIS packs busbars, breakers, disconnects, earthing switches and transformers into a sealed, SF6-filled metal enclosure — 10-20% the footprint of a conventional air-insulated substation. Key components, why it's used, and where.

item.title: IECEx / ATEX Zones vs NEC Class & Division: Hazardous Area Classification
item.description: How the IEC 60079 / ATEX Zone system (Zone 0/1/2, 20/21/22) compares to the North American NEC Class & Division system — equivalency table, gas/dust groups, temperature classes and Ex protection types explained.

item.title: Motor Starting Methods: DOL vs Star-Delta vs Soft Starter vs VFD Compared
item.description: Why starting current matters, how DOL, star-delta, soft starters and VFDs each tame it differently, and a side-by-side comparison of current, torque, cost and complexity.

item.title: MPPT vs PWM Solar Charge Controllers: What Actually Changes
item.description: Why an MPPT controller can pull 20-30% more power than PWM from the same panel, when PWM is still the right call.

item.title: PLC vs DDC: What Actually Separates Them
item.description: PLC and DDC controllers both automate equipment, but they're built for different jobs.

item.title: Sensible vs. Latent Heat: Why Cooling Load Isn't Just Temperature
item.description: Why a cooling load calculation has two separate halves, what sensible and latent heat each actually cool, typical splits by space type.

item.title: P&ID Instrument Bubbles: Line Types & Tag Anatomy Explained
item.description: What the line under an instrument bubble actually means — field-mounted, control-room-mounted, or not directly accessible — plus how to break down a tag like TT01 into loop number, measured variable and device function using ISA S5.1.

item.title: Legend Sheet in a P&ID Explained
item.description: A legend sheet is the reference table that defines every symbol, line type, abbreviation and tag format used on a P&ID — the reason engineers, operators and contractors all read the same drawing the same way.

item.title: P&ID (Piping & Instrumentation Diagram) Explained
item.description: How to actually read a P&ID — equipment, piping, valves, instrumentation tags, and signal lines — plus the ISA tag-naming logic and how a P&ID differs from a PFD.

item.title: Transformer Vector Groups Explained
item.description: How to decode a Dyn11 nameplate, read clock notation, and use vector group to decide whether two transformers can safely parallel — plus a quick-reference table of common groups.

item.title: Chiller Machine: Main Parts & Functions
item.description: Every major chiller component explained — compressor, condenser, evaporator, EXV and 14 more — plus the refrigeration cycle, the chilled water circuit, and air-cooled vs water-cooled chillers compared.

item.title: Chilled Water HVAC Systems: How the Loop Actually Works
item.description: How a chilled water HVAC system moves heat from occupied zones all the way out to atmosphere.

item.title: HVAC System Components Explained
item.description: How an HVAC system actually conditions a space, component by component — compressor, condenser, expansion device, evaporator, air handler, ductwork, and controls.

item.title: Electrical Panel Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): The Complete Checklist
item.description: The 8 stages of an LV panel FAT — visual and mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, hi-pot, functional, protection and interlock tests, and documentation — plus the acceptance criteria that close it out.

item.title: Pre-Commissioning vs Commissioning: What's the Difference
item.description: Pre-commissioning happens before a system is energized; commissioning happens after. The checks each phase actually covers, why the order matters, and where FAT and SAT fit in.

item.title: Star (Y) and Delta (Δ) Connections Explained
item.description: How Star (Y) and Delta (Δ) three-phase winding connections actually differ — the neutral point, the line/phase voltage and current relationships, terminal wiring, and why a Star-Delta starter switches between the two.

item.title: Ingress Protection (IP) Ratings Explained
item.description: How an IP rating is actually built — the solid-protection digit, the liquid-protection digit, and the optional letters — decoded digit by digit against IEC 60529, with a full ratings reference and an IP-to-NEMA cross-check.

item.title: Junction Boxes Explained: Types, Parts & Ratings
item.description: What a junction box actually does, the main types — pull box, gang box, weatherproof, explosion-proof, conduit body, terminal box, panel enclosure — its parts, a material and rating reference, box-fill sizing, and a selection checklist.

item.title: 4-20mA Current Loops: Why Industry Still Trusts an Analog Signal
item.description: Why 4-20mA beat 0-20mA and voltage signals for instrumentation, what live-zero actually protects against, how to convert a reading back to engineering units.

item.title: Control Valve Components Explained
item.description: What every part of a control valve actually does — body, trim (plug & seat), stem, packing, bonnet, actuator, and positioner — component by component, in the order a signal turns into a throttled flow.

item.title: Cavitation vs. Flashing in Control Valves: What's the Difference?
item.description: Cavitation and flashing both start with the same vapor-pressure event inside a control valve — what happens downstream is what makes one loud and pitted, and the other quiet and eroded.

item.title: Control Valve Cv Sizing: Why Oversizing Is the Most Common Mistake
item.description: Basic incompressible-flow control valve Cv sizing, and why an oversized valve hurts controllability even when it comfortably passes the required flow.

item.title: Erosional vs. Economic Velocity: Which One Actually Sizes Your Pipe?
item.description: Two different velocity limits compete to size a process line — economic velocity minimizes lifecycle cost, the API RP 14E erosional velocity protects the pipe wall. The lower of the two always governs.

item.title: Conventional vs. Balanced Bellows vs. Pilot-Operated PSV: Choosing a Relief Valve Type
item.description: Three ways a pressure relief valve holds its disc shut until set pressure — how back pressure, operating margin, and dirty service tolerance decide between a conventional, balanced bellows, or pilot-operated PSV.

item.title: Pipe Routing Guide: 13 Rules Every Layout Should Follow
item.description: Pipe routing principles, pump suction line routing, equipment clearance, pipe racks, supports, dead legs, expansion loops, hot/cold line routing, utility routing, underground vs above ground, nozzle orientation, flange accessibility, and maintenance clearances.

item.title: Power Transformer, CT & PT: Internal Construction
item.description: The internal construction of a power transformer, a current transformer (CT), and a potential transformer (PT/VT) — parts, typical ratings, accuracy classes, and a side-by-side comparison.

item.title: Battery SoC vs DoD: Why They're Not the Same Number
item.description: Why SoC and DoD are two views of the same battery, how SoC is actually estimated in the field, and why chemistry sets the DoD limit that protects cycle life.
